The difference

A clause can be acceptable alone — and risky in combination.

TriageCounsel evaluates configured relationships between independently established contract facts. Here, the system does not stop after reviewing each provision separately. It identifies that the provisions must be considered together and routes the combined position for the appropriate action.

Cross-policy interaction · Limitation of Liability × Indemnification
On this agreement, the Limitation of Liability clause treats gross-negligence claims ambiguously while the Indemnification clause exposes the Provider without a matching carve-out. Neither provision resolves the question on its own — TriageCounsel identifies that they must be read together and routes the combined position to review, rather than letting either clause’s individual result stand alone.

When the contract changes

Change the contract, and TriageCounsel knows which conclusions can no longer be trusted.

Contract review is not static. When a lawyer changes a provision involved in a cross-policy interaction, TriageCounsel does not silently leave the old conclusion marked as valid.

Changed provision
→
Dependent interaction invalidated
→
Reconfirmation required
Unrelated decisions remain intact.
